SUBJECT: Tentative Tract Map No. 84531

PROJECT PROPOSAL/REQUEST
Consideration of a Vesting Tentative Tract Map (TTM) to allow the subdivision of one parcel into a 54-
unit residential condominium development located at 10130 Adella Avenue, within the Industrial Flex (IF)
zone in the Tweedy Boulevard Specific Plan.

PROJECT OVERVIEW

•  General Plan Designation: Industrial
•  Zoning:  Tweedy Boulevard Specific Plan (TBSP); Industrial Flex (IF)
•  Project Location:  10130 Adella Avenue
•  Assessor’s Parcel Number: 6221-026-020
•  Applicant:  Nick Patterson (City Ventures), on behalf of South Gate 1 Inv, LLC

BACKGROUND
Site Characteristics: The subject property is a vacant lot measuring approximately 2.02 acres, located at the
intersection of Adella Avenue and Legacy Lane, within the Tweedy Boulevard Specific Plan area. The
subject site is a relatively flat, rectangular shaped undeveloped property, and primarily comprised of ruderal
vegetation and coarse fill. Fencing currently surrounds the subject site.

Surroundings: The site is surrounded by a mix of residential, commercial, and institutional uses, with Adella
Avenue and Legacy Lane providing primary access. Legacy High School and the Legacy High School
Softball Fields are located directly north of the subject property, across the street from Legacy Lane. There
is an adjoining light industrial/commercial-truck yard directly east of the subject property, and the Los
Angeles River and 710 Freeway further east. Directly south of the subject property, there is a Southern
California Edison (SCE) utility easement with overhead power lines in place, and single-family residential
uses are located south of the SCE easement, within the TBSP. Immediately west of the Project site are
Legacy Lane and Adella Avenue. North of Legacy Lane and west of Adella Avenue are undeveloped lots
within the Legacy High School Complex. South of Legacy Lane and west of Adella Avenue are single-
family residential uses.

Proposed Vesting TTM and Associated Development: The applicant is requesting approval of a Vesting
TTM (Attachment B) to allow the subdivision of one parcel (2.02 acres) into 54 condominium units in
connection with a proposed residential development located at 10130 Adella Avenue.

The proposed development involves the construction of 54 new residential condominium units (for sale),
comprising three-story attached townhomes in six buildings. Each building would contain nine dwelling
units and have a maximum height of approximately 37 feet. The units would consist of a mix of floor plans

with three-to four-bedroom options, ranging in size from 1,304 to 1,705 square feet. Six (12 percent) of the
units would be provided at the moderate-income level.

Administrative Plan Review & Design Review: The proposed (54-unit townhome) development project
associated with the requested Vesting TTM is deemed a “Multifamily Residential” use in accordance with
the provisions of the Zoning Code. “Multifamily Residential” uses are permitted by-right with the approval
of an Administrative Plan Review. In addition, Design Review is required for the proposed development
since it involves a parcel measuring greater than 15,000 square feet. Administrative Plan Review and
Design Review are discretionary procedures conducted by staff. Therefore, the overall design of the
proposed development is not subject to review by the Planning Commission. The Planning Commission
may only take action on the TTM as it relates to the proposed subdivision of a parcel for condominium
purposes to accommodate the proposed development.

ANALYSIS:
Municipal Code Requirements for Vesting TTM Approval: Pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code
(SGMC) Section 12.10.060, the TTM shall be heard by the Planning Commission at a scheduled hearing;
and action shall be taken to approve, conditionally approve, or disapprove such TTM. Subsequently, a Final
Map shall be prepared and forwarded to the City Council for final review, in which they shall approve,
deny, or modify the Planning Commission’s action.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS:
An environmental (air quality, noise, and traffic impact) analysis (Attachment C) was conducted for the
proposed development, and based on the studies, it has been determined the proposed project would qualify
for a Categorical Exemption under CEQA Guidelines Section 15332 (Class 32 – Infill Development
Projects) and would not have a significant environmental impact.

COMMENTS FROM OTHER DEPARTMENTS:
Staff routed the project for comments to several City Departments, including the Public Works Department.
If the project is approved, the comments received from the Public Works Department would be incorporated
as conditions of approval.

RECOMMENDATION:
Based on the evidence presented, Staff recommends that the Planning Commission find that the project is
Categorically Exempt from the CEQA under Section 15332, (Class 32) “Infill Development Projects”,
make the required findings and requirements set forth in the South Gate Municipal Code, and adopt a
Resolution to approve Vesting Tentative Tract Map No. 84531 associated with the 54-unit townhome
development at 10130 Adella Avenue, subject to the recommended conditions of approval stipulated in the
proposed Resolution and/or other conditions that the Planning Commission may wish to impose.

A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF SOUTH GATE PLANNING COMMISSION APPROVING

  WHEREAS, Nick Patterson, on behalf of City Ventures (the "Applicant"), filed a complete
application requesting approval of a Vesting Tentative Tract Map (TTM) to allow the subdivision of one
parcel into 54 condominium units in connection with a proposed residential development located at 10130
Adella Avenue (the "Project"); and

  WHEREAS, the Project site comprises approximately 2.02 acres, identified as Assessor’s Parcel
Number 6221-026-020, and is located within the Industrial Flex (IF) zone of the Tweedy Boulevard
Specific Plan (TBSP) area; and

  WHEREAS, the Project involves new construction of 54 residential condominium units (for sale),
comprising three-story attached townhomes in six buildings, and six (12 percent) of the units will be
provided to moderate-income buyers; and

  WHEREAS, Pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code (SGMC) Section 12.10.060, the Vesting
TTM shall be heard by the Planning Commission at a scheduled hearing; and action shall be taken to
approve, conditionally approve, or disapprove such TTM; and

  WHEREAS, notice of the Planning Commission public hearing of March 18, 2025, was published
in compliance with State law in a local newspaper of general circulation. In addition, a public notice was
mailed 10 days in advance of the hearing to each property owner, occupants and resident within a 1,000-
foot radius of the project site, indicating the date and time of the public hearing in accordance with
California Government Code 65091; and

  WHEREAS, on March 18, 2025 the Planning Commission held a public hearing to receive public
testimony and other evidence regarding the Vesting TTM, including without limitation, information
provided to the Planning Commission by City staff and public testimony; and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission reviewed the Project’s environmental impacts under the
California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and determined the Project qualifies for a Categorical
Exemption under Section 15332 (Class 32 – Infill Development Projects) of the CEQA Guidelines; and

  WHEREAS, this Resolution and its findings are made based upon evidence presented to the
Commission at its public hearing including, without limitation, the staff report submitted by the Community
Development Department; and

  WHEREAS, all legal prerequisites to the adoption of this Resolution have been met.

NOW, THEREFORE, THE PLANNING COMMISSION DOES HEREBY FIND, DETERMINE
AND DECLARE AS FOLLOWS:

SECTION 1.  All of the facts set forth in the recitals are true and correct and are incorporated herein by
reference.

SECTION 3. The Planning Commission reviewed the project’s environmental impacts under the

ENVIRONMENTAL EVALUATION
In accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), the Director’s
determination qualifies for a categorical exemption under CEQA Guidelines Section 15321, (Class
21) “Enforcement Actions by Regulatory Agencies,” in that the City is enforcing the South Gate
Municipal Code.

The Planning Commission’s determination on the termination of the legal, non-conforming use of
the subject property is not subject to California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review
because it is not an “approval” as defined in California Code of Regulations, Title 14, Section
15352, but rather a determination of whether a use must terminate at a site, and therefore does not
commit the City to any definite course of action regarding new uses or changes to the approved
use of the subject property. Furthermore, CEQA does not apply to projects which a public agency
rejects or disapproves pursuant to Section 15270(a).

BACKGROUND
This is an appeal by the applicant, Somos Law Group (“Somos”), on behalf of the property owner,
Alameda Engle Properties, LLC (“AEP” represented by Jason Engle), for a 6.78-acre property
located at 8530 Alameda Street. Somos is appealing the Director of Community Development’s
decision that the legal, nonconforming use for metal processing and/or recycling activities at the
subject property has been abandoned and can no longer be conducted, and the use of the site for
truck trailer storage as a principal use unrelated to metal processing/recycling activities is not a
legal, nonconforming use and must be immediately terminated. Somos is also requesting to change
the zoning of the subject property from IF (Industrial Flex) to M3 (Heavy Manufacturing) and
remove the subject property from the South Gate College District as shown in the Community
Design Element of the General Plan.

It should be noted that AEP also owns the abutting 2.9-acre site to the north at 8440 S. Alameda
Street, which is located outside of the City and in the County of Los Angeles. Access to both
properties is via a driveway from Alameda Street to the property at 8440 S. Alameda Street. This
property is also being used for truck trailer storage and according to County staff, a conditional
use permit (CUP) is currently being processed.

History of Zoning and Land Use of Subject Property
As early as 1961, the Subject Property was designated as being within a Heavy Manufacturing
(“M-3”) Zone.

ANALYSIS:

Appeal of Director’s Determination
On January 21, 2025, the City sent a Director’s Determination and Noncompliance Notification
letter to the applicant indicating the legal, nonconforming use of the Subject Property for metal
processing and/or recycling activities – including the integral truck trailer storage component of
those activities – has been determined to be abandoned and can no longer be conducted at the Site
unless otherwise in conformity to all current laws and regulations of the City (and applicable
governmental agencies). Furthermore, based on staff’s research and information provided by
Somos, the use of the Site for truck trailer storage as a principal use unrelated to metal
processing/recycling activities is not a legal, nonconforming use – and, as such, must be
immediately terminated.

On February 6, 2025, the applicant filed an appeal requesting the Planning Commission
challenging the Director’s determination based on the following grounds:

1. The Director’s Determination is unsupported by the South Gate Municipal Code (SGMC)
  purportedly due to the Director’s differentiation between an ancillary and primary use, that the
  immediate termination of a legal, nonconforming use is inconsistent with the SGMC and
  General Plan, and the Determination violates procedural requirements;
2. Substantive and procedural due process concerns; and
3. Termination of a legal, nonconforming use is a de facto regulatory taking; and,
4. The City’s failure to comply with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), Public
  Resources Code Section 21000, et seq.

Truck Storage/Terminal Use: AEP and its tenant have been using the subject property to store
trucks, truck-trailers, and storage containers. Under the SGMC, this use is defined as “truck
storage/terminal” use which, pursuant to the SGMC Section 11.60.230 “T” definitions, “means
indoor or outdoor site for freight, truck terminals, truck storage yards, or similar commercial
facilities.”

SGMC Prohibits that Use at 8530 Alameda Street: The subject property is zoned Industrial Flex
(IF). Table 11.21-3, under SGMC Section 11.21.030 “Land use permissions tables,” lists allowed
land uses within the IF zone. Truck storage/terminal use is not listed on that Table as an allowed

   use within the IF zone. SGMC Section 11.21.020 notes that “Any land use that is not specifically
  listed in the land use tables for the applicable zone shall not be allowed or permitted within the
  zone.” Therefore, the storage of trucks, truck-trailers and containers is a prohibited use in the IF
  zone.

  It is undisputed that the recycling/metal processing activities that occurred at the subject property
  were legal, nonconforming, and that truck trailer storage is not currently a permitted use at the
  subject property pursuant to the South Gate Municipal Code (inclusive of the Zoning Code). The
  issues of contention are (i) whether the legal, nonconforming recycling/metal processing activities
  at the subject property have been abandoned; and/or (ii) whether the appellant has submitted
  sufficient evidence to substantiate that the current use of the site for truck trailer storage unrelated
  to recycling/metal processing activities constitutes a legal, nonconforming use of the subject
  property.

  In response to the appellant’s arguments set forth in the Request for Appeal, Staff submits the
  following.

  ASSERTION: The Director’s Determination is unsupported by the South Gate Municipal
  Code.
  The appellant first argues that the Director failed to make a determination that the legal,
  nonconforming use is “wholly discontinued or abandoned for a continuous period of two calendar
  years” as required by SGMC 11.55.040(D). The Director, however, correctly determined that the
  legal, nonconforming recycling/metal processing use at the site was wholly discontinued and/or
  abandoned – as evidenced by the cessation of all activities associated with the recycling/metal
  processing activities in or around 2020, including the demolition of the structure that was
  previously utilized for such activities. Contrary to the appellant’s contention, the Director did not
  distinguish between primary and ancillary legal, non-conforming uses. Rather, the Director
  accepted the appellants assertion that the storage of truck trailers at the site was an “integral part
  of metal processing operations,” however, the Director did determine that the truck trailer storage
  was only done as part of the recycling/metal processing activities while those activities were
  occurring. The Director correctly determined that the current use of the site for truck trailer storage
  only is NOT a continuation of the use of the trucks for the recycling/metal processing activities,
  and, is, in fact, a wholly new use.

  The appellant also argues that the immediate termination of the truck trailer storage is inconsistent
  with the South Gate Municipal Code and the General Plan – which the appellant contends promotes
  a more gradual transition to a conforming use. However, the appellant fails to recognize that it
  was the appellant’s abandonment of the recycling/metal processing activities for more than 2 years
  that resulted in the termination of its legal, nonconforming rights – and not any action by the City.
  The City’s requirement that the legal, nonconforming use be terminated for 2 continuous years
  does, in fact, provide for a gradual transition – but the appellant failed to utilize those 2 years to
  make a transition to a conforming use. Instead, the appellant transitioned to using the subject
  property for the prohibited truck trailer storage use.

   The appellant further mistakenly argues that the Director failed to make findings required by
  Section 11.55.040(D) of the municipal code. Specifically, the appellant argues that the Director

  discontinue use of the nonconforming structure is apparent, as determined by the director”

  discontinue/abandon a nonconforming structure – and not the owner’s intent to discontinue a legal,
  nonconforming use. That being said, the Director determined that the structure previously existing
  at the site was voluntarily demolished in or around March 2020 – and that all other activities
  associated with the recycling/metal processing use also terminated around the same time. The
  Director also determined that all other equipment, furnishings, and the structure itself used for the
  recycling/metal processing activities have been absent from the site for more than two years.
  Moreover, no additional business licenses have been acquired for recycling/metal processing
  activities for at least 2 years. Any continued utility use at the site (including electricity, gas, water
  or waste collection) does not negate the Director’s determination that all use of the subject property
  for recycling/metal processing activities has been abandoned/discontinued for more than 2 years.

  substantive and procedural due process concerns.
  The appellant contends that the manner in which the City has handled requests from appellant’s
  legal counsel has raised concerns regarding the appellant’s substantive and procedural due process.
  Appellant also apparently incorrectly argues that the Director suggested that the appellant was
  required to obtain a Conditional Use Permit in 1988 as a result of a change in the City’s Zoning
  Code. Lastly, appellant argues that Staff has been slow to acknowledge or process its request for
  a Zone Change and General Plan Amendment. It should be noted that Staff provided documents
  in its possession – however, was not required to provide copies of business licenses which were
  no longer in the possession of the City. [Business licenses are issued to business operators – and
  the appellant would have been in the best position to retain the prior business licenses.] Moreover,
  the Director did not assert that the appellant required a Conditional Use Permit, but rather that the
  change in the City’s Zoning Code requiring a Conditional Use Permit for the recycling/metal
  processing use of the site is what converted the legal status of recycling/metal processing use of
  the site to “legal, nonconforming”. Lastly, the processing of the Zone Change and General Plan

  processing of those requests are not related to the Director’s Determination regarding the
  termination of the legal, nonconforming status of the recycling/metal processing activities or the
  lack of such status for the truck trailer storage.

  ASSERTION: Termination of the legal nonconforming use is a de facto regulatory taking.
  The appellant contends that the changes to the City’s Zoning laws and General Plan amount to a
  regulatory taking because of the limited uses allowed at the subject property. However, the City
  provides for the continuation of nonconforming uses – and, as such, appellant would have been
  allowed to continue the recycling/metal processing use of the site had the appellant not abandoned
  the use or otherwise caused the termination of the use as set forth in SGMC Chapter 11.55. It is

  The appellant incorrectly asserts that the City’s termination of the legal, nonconforming use of the

  Staff recommends the Planning Commission uphold the Director’s Determination that the legal,

following findings:

  2020 for recycling/metal processing activities. Although the main metal processing

  the processed metal thereafter – which necessitated said trucks being parked and/or

  for recycling facilities – thereby making the recycling/metal processing use at the

  3. On or about April 28, 2015, the City Council adopted Ordinance 2323, which further
  amended the South Gate Zoning Code and changed the zoning designation of the
  Subject Property to Industrial Flex (“IF”) Zone – thereby further making the
  recycling/metal processing use at the Subject Property legal, nonconforming.
  4. In or around March 2020, the owner of the Subject Property, AEP, voluntarily
  demolished the structure that was used for the recycling/metal processing activities,
  and all other activities associated with the recycling/metal processing use ceased at that
  time.
  5. In or around March 2020, Fleet Yards, Inc. (“Fleet”) commenced utilizing the Subject
  Property for the storage of truck trailers and/or containers as a principal use not related
  to any recycling/metal processing activities.

On May 2, 2023, the South Gate Planning Commission  conducted  a public hearing on the request  by Alameda

TUP. AEP has now asked to appeal that decision to the South Gate City Council.  For the reasons explained  by
the City Attorney's  Office  at the May 2, Planning Commission  meeting  and reiterated  below, an appeal of this
matter to the City Council  is not available.

As the City has repeatedly  advised AEP and Fleet Yards, the TUP was initially  issued in error, because it
purported  to allow a "temporary"  use of the Premises for a period of at least one year and possibly as many as

name implies, are intended  to allow only short-term  uses of land.  Specifically,  Section 11.51.070  of the  Zoning

Code states that the maximum  duration  of a temporary  use permit  shall not exceed three days in a row or ten
days in any calendar  year.  It is unfortunate  that the TUP was erroneously  issued in 2020 for a much longer one-
year period and erroneously  renewed  in 2021 for an additional  one-year  period.  But those earlier errors do not
entitle AEP to further  extensions  of the TUP for periods  far in excess of the maximum  durations  authorized  by
the Zoning Code. Simply put, there is no authority  in the Zoning Code for issuing or renewing  a temporary  use

permit for any period longer than three consecutive  days or ten days in any calendar year.

Furthermore,  the original  issuance of the TUP in violation  of the Zoning Code aiso meant that the City was not
required  to grant AEP a hearing on the matter  of renewing  the TUP. Again, as publicly stated by the City's legal

ENVIRONMENTAL EVALUATION: The California Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA"), codified at
California Public Resources Code§§ 21000 et seq., requires the City to consider the potential environmental
impacts of any project which the City is asked to approve. State regulations known as the "CEQA Guidelines",
codified at Division 6 of Title 14 of the California Code of Regulations, provide a number of "categorical
exemptions" for activities which are not deemed to be projects under CEQA or which are otherwise not subject
to CEQA. In the present case, the matter before the City Council is exempt from CEQA pursuant to a Class l
exemption set forth in Section 15301 of the CEQA Guidelines. Class 1 exemptions apply to the operation, repair,
maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing, or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities,
mechanical equipment, or topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of existing or fo1mer use.
Here, the Planning Commission is being asked to approve or deny a license to continue the existing or former use
of the licensed facility and is therefore a matter covered by the Class l exception.

BACKGROUND: This is an appeal by Jason Engle on behalf of Alameda Engle Properties, LLC, the owner of
property located at 8530 Alameda Street. Mr. Engle is appealing the Director of Community Development's
decision to deny an extension or renewal of Temporary Use Permit 2020-01. The history of that Temporary Use
Permit is as follows:

The City's Business License Department shows business license records (Attachment B) for "Jack Engle Co,"
which statted business on Ap1il 18, 1977, and closed business on March 27, 2020, at 8530 Alameda Street. This

Street,"  with  six conditions  of approval.  A July  16, 2020  letter  from  the City's  former  Director  of Community
Development,  setting  forth  those conditions  of approval  for that pertnit,  is attached  hereto  as Attachment  C. As
of the appeal date, the appellant  has failed  to comply  with  the required  conditions  of approval  and has also been
operating  without  a city business  license.

The  appellant  applied  for  a "renewal"  of Temporary  Use Permit  2020-01  on July  11, 2022.  For the reasons

otherwise  unauthorized  uses to be conducted  for a few days, not for multi-year  periods.

Past/Proposed  Use of Property  is as a "Truck  Storage/Terminal":  Applicant  and its tenant  have been using  the

outdoor  site for freight,  truck  terminals,  truck  storage  yards,  or similar  commercial  facilities."

11.21-3,  under  SGMC  Section  11.21.030  "Land  use pernnissions  tables",  lists  allowed  land uses within  the IF
zone. Truck  storage/teiminal  use is not listed  on that Table  as an allowed  use within  the IF zone.  SGMC  Section
11.21.020  notes that "Any  land use that is not specifically  listed in the land use tables for the applicable  zone shall
not be allowed  or permitted  within  the zone."  Therefore,  the storage  of trucks,  truck-trailers  and containers  is a
prohibited  use in the IF zone.

Temporary  Use Pertnits  Cannot  Authorize  Prohibited  Uses for Extended  Durations.  Pursuant  to SGMC  Section
11.51.070  "Temporary  Use Permit,"  temporary  use permits  are processed  administratively  to "allow  for short-
term  activities  that warrant  individual  consideration  and are acceptable  because  of their  temporary,  short-tertn

appeal is the subject  of the above-referenced  hearing.

In 1988, the City amended its Zoning Code, in part, to require a Conditional Use Permit for

Zoning Map Amendment and General Plan Amendment
The applicant is requesting to change the zoning of the property at 8530 Alameda Street from IF
to M3 and remove the subject property from the South Gate College District as shown in the
Community Design Element of the General Plan. The request is to accommodate Fleet Yards,
Inc.’s operation as a truck storage/terminal facility.

Around 2015, the City rezoned properties in the area from M3 to IF. This was to accommodate
future growth of the East Los Angeles Community College (ELACC) within the South Gate
College District as described in the Community Design Element of the City’s General Plan. The
subject property is included in the South Gate College District as part of sub-area 1 (portions north
of Firestone Boulevard and east of Alameda Street). ELACC anticipates a largely expanded
campus complex that would include adaptive reuse of nearby industrial facilities along Firestone
Boulevard. Changing the zone to M3 would be contrary to the vision and policies of the General

   Based on our coordination with the City and prior conversations with you, we
understand that a GPA or ZC/GPA are the most efficient and practical paths forward to
formalize the long-standing industrial use at the Property.

  As outlined in the application, this request for a ZC and GPA is consistent with all

  1. The ZC ad GPA Prevents Challenges Re Use Continuity and
  Consistency

  The City rezoned the portion of the Property in South Gate from M3 to Industrial
Flex “IF” in 2015. As depicted in the Property Map below, nearly one-third of the
property (including the only point of ingress/egress) is located outside the City in
unincorporated Los Angeles County (“County”). The portion of the Property located in
the County is zoned “M2” for Heavy Manufacturing uses. The entirety of the Property
has been used for truck trailer and container storage for over 50 years in the City of
South Gate and over 60 years on the County side. The ZC and GPA approval will
formalize consistent zoning and uses across the entirety of the Property. Split zoning
over a single property, and/or inconsistencies in permitted uses between the northern
(County) portion of the property and southern (City) portion of the property, together with
the single point of ingress and egress severely restrict the scope viable alternative uses.
The Proposed ZC ad GPA will enable use consistency over both portions of the
Property and avoid additional challenges in implementing future uses.

  2. The ZC & GPA are Consistent with Uses in the Surrounding Area.

  As depicted in the Site Map, the surrounding uses are predominantly

parking, truck repair facilities to the north, and an auto auction facility, auto parts facility,
and metal manufacturing facility to the west. The residential development to the
northeast of the Property is separated by railroad tracks and additional truck parking
facilities that are not owned, operated or affiliated with AEP. The ZC and GPA revert the
current zoning to the previous “M3” zoning designation, which is consistent with the
surrounding industrial uses, and will allow the property to continue to operate as a vital
part of the local economy without increasing the intensity of the use.

  3. The ZC & GPA Facilitate Productive Use of the Property While the
  City Evaluates City-Wide Land Use & Policy Changes

  The Property’s unique characteristics, including its location in multiple
jurisdictions, split zoning designations, and location adjacent to railway and heavy
industrial uses substantially narrow the scope of viable alternative uses. If the historic
use is not allowed to continue as a “bridge” to future regional redevelopment options,
